claims.text: NiCoFeCrMn high-entropy alloy multilayers can serve as a transition material between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
Controlled deposition parameters can systematically vary interface coherency in NiCoFeCrMn multilayers.
The initial NiCoFeCrMn multilayer has a coherent interface.
Sputtering pressure can be used to vary interface coherency.
Substrate temperature can be used to vary interface coherency.
The proposed creep conditions are 800 °C and 500 MPa.
Interface coherency is the structural mediator controlling creep behavior.
Variation of interface coherency causes a transition from diffusion-mediated to dislocation-mediated creep.
The proposed material will exhibit a 30% increase in creep resistance relative to a multilayer with an incoherent interface.
Creep resistance is to be evaluated using creep strain rate in s^-1.
The baseline is a NiCoFeCrMn multilayer with an incoherent interface.
An interface coherency ratio of 0.8 defines the relevant boundary.
The exact relationship between interface coherency and creep behavior remains unclear.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome claims increased creep resistance, which ordinarily corresponds to a lower creep strain rate, whereas the falsification rule treats an increase of at least 20% in creep strain rate as confirmation. The directions of improvement are therefore inconsistent.

The outcome states a 30% increase in creep resistance but describes that resistance as being measured directly in creep strain-rate units. Creep strain rate is a creep-response metric and normally varies inversely with creep resistance, so the stated direction is ambiguous.
